answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it may trade, with the stake slashed when peers attest bad behaviour. Like a ledge that narrows the path into a busy inlet, the cost makes mass fake identities uneconomical, while honest agents keep working. Reputation then accumulates slowly, like sediment carried toward the ocean, so a newcomer cannot buy instant trust and a swarm of fresh accounts cannot outvote established participants.
